subject: Event lead schema and post-processing for September roadshows
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightcon.com>, EventPro Ops <ops@eventpro.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Event lead schema and post-processing for September roadshows

Hi Elena / EventPro team,

Thanks again for taking time to align on the lead handoff. To make the integration smooth for our roadshows in Sept/Oct, I put together a minimal schema and some post-processing rules so we can guarantee GDPR-friendly opt-in handling and deterministic dedupe before HubSpot ingest. Attached: redwood_event_field_mapping_v1.csv (proposed field map) and consent_snippet_v3.docx (short opt-in copy + timestamps).

High level ask: can you confirm the following by EOD Tuesday?
- Which event ID will be present on the CSV export ("event_id" vs "venue_code")
- Whether the badge scan payload includes a UTC timestamp and device_id
- How you surface explicit opt-in (checkbox vs form redirect param)

Our constraints:
- We need a per-event consent token to be stored as a contact property so we can honor deletion/retention requests.
- We will run a light postprocess pipeline that: normalize phone/email, apply prefix KV caching for duplicate badge reads (30s window), map and upsert into HubSpot; fallback to Salesforce for a small set of strategic accounts.

If it helps, EventPro can send a sample export and we can mock the exact transform on our side. Proposed next step: Elena sends a 100-row sample CSV and we confirm mapping + a short smoke test ingestion.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Manager, Field Marketing Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_event_field_mapping_v1.csv (CSV mapping), consent_snippet_v3.docx (word doc)

From: Elena Morales <elena@brightcon.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: EventPro Ops <ops@eventpro.io>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Event lead schema and post-processing for September roadshows

Sean — thanks, this is helpful. See attached eventpro_export_sample.json which is a sanitized export from our scanning devices at last month's show. Quick answers:
- event_id is present as "event_code" in our export (we can alias to "event_id")
- timestamps are in UTC, ISO8601 under "scan_time"
- opt-in is captured two ways: checkbox on the tablet (opt_in=true) and a redirect param if the attendee fills the follow-up form (redirect=1). For badge-only scans we can add an "explicit_consent=false" flag unless the checkbox was checked.

Couple of questions on your end:
1) For the per-event consent token you mentioned — do you want us to include a hashed token in the export or would Redwood generate one on ingest?
2) We occasionally have badge duplicates when attendees roam between booths. Is the 30s dedupe window configurable? Our devices sometimes lag up to 45s in crowded halls.

We attached the sample export and highlighted the relevant columns. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the JSON.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Partnerships 
BrightCon Events

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Event lead schema and post-processing for September roadshows

Sean / team — looping in ops to confirm implementation details and ownership. I reviewed Elena's sample and sketched a 3-step postprocess we can run in the ingestion pipeline:

1) Normalize & enrich (Marissa owns):
   - Normalize phone and email (E.164 + lowercase)
   - Map event_code -> event_id and add "source=badge-scan" property
   - If scan_time present, convert to contact property "last_seen_utc"

2) Consent token & retention (Olga owns):
   - If opt_in=true OR redirect=1 then set contact property "consent=true" and store consent_token=SHA256(event_id + contact_email + scan_time)
   - If explicit_consent=false, mark record "consent=false" and route to nurture list only; do not send marketing emails
   - Add audit log record for each consent decision with timestamp and device_id

3) Dedup & upsert (Ben owns):
   - Apply time-window dedupe: default 30s, configurable per-event (Ben will expose config flag)
   - For contacts matching existing customers in SFDC (company domain allowlist), route upsert to Salesforce instead of HubSpot
   - Attach original export file reference to contact timeline (link to Drive)

Action items:
- Ben: add per-event dedupe config and test with a 45s window on sample file (due 2026-09-04)
- Olga: confirm consent_token schema and retention TTL (suggest 24 months) by 2026-09-03
- Sean: confirm final mapping and confirm whether we should generate consent_token on ingest or accept pre-hashed token from EventPro (reply here)

Marissa
Sr. Field Ops Program Manager

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Event lead schema and post-processing for September roadshows

All — quick status update from my side after spinning up a dev job against the sample. TL;DR: we can support both options for the consent token but recommend Redwood generate it on ingest to avoid relying on vendor hashing practices. Notes:
- Dedupe: adjustable window; default 30s, tested with 45s and 60s. For crowded halls I'd recommend 45s as a safe middle ground.
- HubSpot mapping: I mapped event_code -> custom property "event_id__c" and confirmed HubSpot accepts the upload; we'll add the contact property "consent_token" and "consent_source".
- SFDC fallback: I validated upsert for two sample domains; mapping looks OK but will need a final field-level security review.

Next steps:
1) Sean: confirm we will generate the consent_token on ingest (if yes, I'll finalize code and deploy to staging)
2) Elena/EventPro: send the full 100-row sample CSV (ops@eventpro.io) so I can run a larger smoke test
3) Olga: once you confirm TTL, I'll wire the audit-log event to our ingestion trace

I'll push a staging job today and share logs.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Lead Field Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: eventpro_export_sample.json (from BrightCon), redwood_event_field_mapping_v1.csv (proposed), consent_snippet_v3.docx
